R6K-bear-walk-0001.name: 160 m N of Sphaler Creek
R6K-bear-walk-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R6K-bear-walk-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2019 (fire R90918), 230 m SW: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 31 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Sphaler Creek 160 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Stewart, about 170 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 57.04704, -131.21108, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 460 m N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 79 m, about 17 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-21, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
